hints: Exclusive-or the whole row. The pairs cancel, so what is left is the exclusive-or of the two lonely values - which is not either of them.
That result is not useless, though: every bit set in it is a bit where the two lonely values *differ*.
Pick any one of those bits. Every value in the row either has it or does not, and the two lonely values are on opposite sides of that split.
So xor the row twice more, once per side - and within each side, one lonely value survives while every pair cancels, because both members of a pair fall on the same side.
